intro: What this version does not do yet, with how often it matters, measured on the graphs of the five organisms built with Ensembl 115 (every number is a count over Ensembl's own records of the releases asked about, not over a benchmark's judgement):
items: Without a release, a string is what it means today …
Across an assembly change, places are compared through Ensembl's own mapping of the two assemblies, and only where Ensembl publishes one.
Copies on patches and alternative loci are placed by Ensembl's assembly exceptions.
A number written with a version that two numbering schemes share is read where its version exists.
A gene's own continuation does not outrank a branch that left it while it lived on.
An id that Ensembl retired and later brought back with an old version is one node with two lives.
At its own release, a symbol of the organism's name authority can answer another gene …
A name in one letter case that a link of another gene spells exactly so answers that gene, not the gene the name authority displays with it in mixed case.
A gene that Ensembl retired without a successor can answer another gene than the one that holds its accessions today.
A gene whose history splits, converted to an external database, answers no identifier where the first-ranked of its descendants has none, although another descendant has one.
In mouse releases 80 and 81, RefSeq_mRNA also holds predicted and RefSeqGene accessions.
The support of a name counts a database that writes it in another letter case.
